title: Political will, partnerships needed to achieve SDGs
summary: With only less than half of the Sustainable Development Goals progressing as planned, President Marcos yesterday called for political will and enhanced partnerships to meet the targets requiring…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on November 16, 2026
PPA Pool photos by Mike Alquinto

MANILA, Philippines — With only less than half of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) progressing as planned, President Marcos yesterday called for political will and enhanced partnerships to meet the targets requiring global action on poverty, inequality and other problems.

In remarks delivered during the 16th Association of Southeast Asian Nations-United Nations (ASEAN-UN) Summit yesterday, Marcos noted that 2030 is less than four years away, but only 36 percent of accessible SDG targets are on track.

“Achieving these goals requires renewed political will, stronger partnerships with the private sector and cooperation that is evidence-based and responsive to the needs of its members, especially developing countries,” Marcos said.
The SDGs are 17 targets calling for a global effort to end poverty and to carry out strategies on improving health and education, reducing inequality and promoting economic growth.
It is in line with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development adopted by all UN member-states in 2015.

The goals include end poverty in all its forms everywhere; end hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture; ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages; ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all; achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls; ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all; ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all; promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all; build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation.

The other SDGs are reduce inequality within and among countries; make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable; ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns; take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts; conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources for sustainable development; protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss; promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development; provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels; strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the Global Partnership for Sustainable Development.

In a statement, the Presidential Communications Office said ASEAN and UN leaders had reaffirmed cooperation under their Plan of Action for 2026-2030, which covers peace and security, digital transformation, climate action, disaster management, health and the protection of women and children.
